newsitem.title: GERMANY: Official says drastic cuts harm German military.
newsitem.headline: Official says drastic cuts harm German military.

text.p: Drastic cuts in Bonn's military budget threaten Germany's ability to carry out effective peacekeeping missions and could create a second-class army, parliament's armed forces ombudswoman said on Tuesday.

Claire Marienfeld said cutbacks were already forcing soldiers to cannibalise intact vehicles for spare parts and skimp on training and troop levels, trends that could end up weakening the armed forces for decades.
"Shrinking finances clash with the growing responsibilities of the armed forces," she said in her annual report. "Proper training of soldiers cannot be allowed to suffer."
Marienfeld said deploying peacekeeping forces in former Yugoslavia last year was in keeping with united Germany's higher profile in world affairs and should not be endangered.

Germany sent 4,000 troops to Croatia and Bosnia for a year on the multinational IFOR mission and another 3,300 are now based in Bosnia with the follow-up SFOR mission, the first time in post-war history that Germany has sent combat troops abroad.
"The successful deployment of German soldiers in the former Yugoslavia...has contributed to the public respect for military service," Marienfeld said.
Taking full part in such international missions had boosted morale among the troops, she said, but poor equipment and more limited training threatened to lower it again.
"We cannot afford to have the perception of a second-class army in the minds of our troops," she said.

Defence Minister Volker Ruehe said the report offered an accurate description of the current condition of the German armed forces and agreed that cuts in training could jeopardise the mission in former Yugoslavia.
